title: account channel — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Negotiated via auth.support/auth_ok.support (capability id afbws.account.channel.v2). Same convention as afbws.alarm.v2/afbws.market: ONE schema id per message (`afbws.account.<op>.v2`, no .request/.response/.push suffixes); the same schema is the request, its response (echoes `request_id`) and, for `list`/`orders`, the server push (a message WITHOUT `request_id`). `events` has no push; `error` is the single typed error. Operations: list, orders, events, cash, set, ledger, settings, error; `list` takes `bf_id` + `account_id`. `bf_id` is the account type for AFB-side accounts: `virtual` (trading simulation) and `bond` (virtual account of a bond portfolio; `account_id = "bond:" + portfolio_id`; created and deleted together with the portfolio, so there is no `open` operation). Operations `cash`, `set`, `ledger`, `settings` serve accounts of type `bond` (the backend answers `not_supported` for other types); each has no server push, so `request_id` is always required. `settings` is deprecated (auto-conversion spread removed; the server answers `unsupported_action`). The money of a `bond` account is held ONLY in its base currency: cash[] has at most one element. `items` are explicit allow-list projections built by backend/trade/public_views.py (never a verbatim proxy of a BF broker.* payload); $defs accountSnapshot/order/eventRecord are this file's own strict shapes , reusing only the field-level $defs of payloads/broker.accounts.json. A multi-currency account (broker / virtual) is expressed through cash[] (one entry per currency); a `bond` account holds money only in its base currency (cash[] has at most one element); the virtual account fills `as_of`. `account` means a broker account (one bf_id may have more than one), not the connector itself.

bfId.description: Connector id (broker `bf_id`) or the type of an AFB-side account: `virtual`, `bond`. Open string: new account types need no schema change.

position.title: Public position projection built by AFB (backend/trade/public_views.py). Own definition, independent of payloads/broker.accounts.json#/$defs/position: BF positions carry only broker_ref {broker, symbol}; AFB restores the optional `instrument` block itself (from its catalog / finam.db).

instrument.description: Instrument block restored by AFB; optional.

instrument_key.description: Catalog instrument key (`MISX:<board>:<secid>`, case-sensitive). Filled by AFB-side accounts (`bond`); optional for broker positions.

accrued_int.description: Accrued coupon interest per unit in the instrument currency (a bond position); null/absent when not applicable.

accountOp.title: One entry of the account operation log (facts only; written by the backend only).
accountOp.description: A light journal of facts: rows are independent (no ids, no links between rows). Decimal strings for money and prices. ALL account money is in the account base currency, so `amount` is always in the base currency; the instrument currency appears only in `price` / `accrued_int` and, when it differs from the base one, in `fx_currency` / `fx_rate`. No spread and no fees. `kind`: deposit | withdraw (user cash movement), buy | sell (emulated at LAST MOEX, by a quantity edit or an auto-sale), coupon | amortization | redemption (income credited by the schedule), reconcile (reserved for a manual or broker-sync correction of a position / cash; amount 0 means position only).

ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC time of the record; for an income row, the time it was credited.

amount.description: Signed cash movement in the account BASE currency, decimal string: negative for buy / withdraw, positive for the rest. For reconcile it is the cash correction (0 = position only).

instrument_key.description: Instrument key. Present for buy / sell / coupon / amortization / redemption / reconcile; absent for deposit / withdraw.

quantity.description: Number of units. Present together with instrument_key; for income rows it is the quantity held at the moment of crediting.

price.description: buy / sell only: clean price per unit in the INSTRUMENT currency (decimal string).

accrued_int.description: buy / sell only: accrued interest per unit in the INSTRUMENT currency (decimal string).

event_date.description: coupon / amortization / redemption only: YYYY-MM-DD payment date by the schedule (used to match the row with the schedule).

fx_currency.description: Present only if the instrument currency differs from the account base currency: the currency the amount was converted from / to.

fx_rate.description: Present together with fx_currency: base-currency units per 1 unit of fx_currency (CETS LAST, decimal string). The amount in the instrument currency is amount / fx_rate.

accountSnapshot.title: One broker account's public projection — see backend/trade/public_views.py::account_snapshot(). Never carries broker_account_id (see payloads/broker.accounts.json — the same field the wire type deliberately dropped).

tradable.description: True only for this bf_id's default (trading) account.

readonly.description: Broker / virtual accounts only (every `bf_id` except `bond`; required there, forbidden for `bond`).

owner.description: `bf_id: bond` only (required there, forbidden for other accounts). Owner of the portfolio account. An EMPTY object `{}` means the account is the caller's own. For a public account of somebody else (read-only for the caller) `name` and `tier` describe the owner; `null` means the owner is unknown.

name.description: Display name of the owner; null — unknown. Absent for the caller's own account.

tier.description: Tier of the owner (e.g. `admin`, `manager`); null — unknown. Absent for the caller's own account.

cash.description: Cash balances, one entry per currency. For `bf_id: bond` account money is held ONLY in the account base currency: at most one element.

order.title: Allow-list projection over payloads/broker.orders.json#/$defs/order plus AFB/frontend-synthesized display fields (client_order_id, cancel_source) that BF never sends — see accountStore.ts::normalizeOrder. `symbol` is not part of the BF wire shape either; it stays optional and is resolved by the frontend from the owning deal when present.

eventRecord.title: Journal of incoming BF events (JSONL direction=in) for one bf_id/day — unchanged from the legacy account/get_events response. See ExecutionService.get_account_events_for_user and event_translator.envelope_to_event_record.

list.title: afbws.account.list.v2 — read accounts (request / response / server push).
list.description: Request (`request_id`, no `items`): optional `bf_id` (only that connector's accounts; omitted = every account of every accessible connector), optional `account_id` (a single account; use together with `bf_id`; replaces v1 `get`), optional `force` (bypass the cached BfRuntimeState.accounts snapshot and re-fetch from BF). Response (same `request_id`, with `items`): only `request_id` + `items[]` (accountSnapshot, possibly empty). Push (no `request_id`, server-initiated): the full account list of ONE `bf_id` — `bf_id`, `default_account_id`, `items[]` (BF's broker.accounts is a full snapshot, never a delta; the virtual account is pushed the same way). For `bf_id: "bond"` (accounts of bond portfolios, `account_id = "bond:" + portfolio_id`): a request without `account_id` returns only the caller's own accounts; with `account_id` the caller's own or a readable public one (staff accounts are `visibility public`, read-only for others). A `bond` snapshot carries `owner` instead of `readonly`: `{}` for the caller's own account, `{name, tier}` of the owner (null when unknown) for somebody else's public one; broker and virtual snapshots carry `readonly` and no `owner`. The snapshot is filled from the account log: `cash[]` per currency, `equity` in the base currency (cash + market value), `tradable: true`, `status: ok`, positions carry `instrument_key` and `accrued_int`. The push for `bond` is event-driven (after `cash` / `set`, an income credit, a composition change), like the virtual account. A request carrying `items`/`default_account_id` or a response/push carrying request-only fields is invalid.

force.description: Request only: bypass the cached accounts snapshot and re-fetch from BF.

orders.title: afbws.account.orders.v2 — orders of one account (request / response / server push).
orders.description: Request (`request_id`, no `items`): `bf_id` required; `account_id` omitted = the connector's default (trading) account (the only account order history is available for, see payloads/broker.orders.json). Response (same `request_id`, with `items`): `bf_id`, `account_id`, `items[]`. Push (no `request_id`, server-initiated): `bf_id`, `account_id`, `items[]` for the default (trading) account.

events.title: afbws.account.events.v2 — journal of incoming BF events for one bf_id/day (request / response).
events.description: Request (`request_id`, no `items`): `bf_id` required, `date` (YYYY-MM-DD market date) omitted = today (market_today()). Response (same `request_id`, with `items`): `bf_id`, `date`, `items[]`. There is NO server push for events: `request_id` is always required.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD market date; omitted in a request means today (market_today()).

cash.title: afbws.account.cash.v2 — deposit or withdraw cash of a `bond` account (request / response).
cash.description: Request: `account_id`, `kind` (deposit | withdraw), `currency`, `amount` (positive decimal string). Account money is held only in the account base currency: `currency` must equal it, otherwise the error is `validation_error`. The backend writes a `deposit` / `withdraw` operation (amount in the base currency); the starting capital is the first deposit. Response (same `request_id`, with `item`): the updated account snapshot. Errors (`afbws.account.error.v2`): `insufficient_cash` (withdraw above the balance), `validation_error` (`currency` differs from the account base currency), `forbidden` (not the owner / not staff for a public account), `not_found`, `not_supported`. No server push (the owner receives `afbws.account.list.v2`).

currency.description: Request only: must equal the account base currency.

set.title: afbws.account.set.v2 — set target quantities of a `bond` account (request / response).
set.description: Request: `account_id`, `targets[]` (1..200, target quantity per instrument key). Each row is executed separately: delta > 0 is an emulated `buy`, delta < 0 a `sell`, both at LAST MOEX; partial success is allowed. Response (same `request_id`): `item` — the account snapshot after the edit — and `rejected[]` (refused rows with `reason`; empty when all went through). A whole-request failure is `afbws.account.error.v2`. No server push.

quantity.description: Target quantity (not a delta); 0 closes the position.

reason.description: no_last_price: no LAST MOEX today; no_fx: no exchange rate to convert the instrument currency to the base one; insufficient_cash: not enough money for a buy; not_in_set: the instrument is not in the portfolio composition; not_supported: instrument class has no provider; forbidden: not allowed for the caller.

ledger.title: afbws.account.ledger.v2 — page of the account operation log (request / response).
ledger.description: Request: `account_id`, optional `before` (opaque cursor string taken from a previous response `next`: return entries older than it), optional `limit` (1..200). Entries are returned newest first (new -> old). Response (same `request_id`, with `items`): `account_id`, `items[]` (accountOp), `next` — the opaque cursor to pass as `before` for the next page, or null at the end. The client must not parse or construct cursors. No server push.

before.description: Request only. Opaque cursor from a previous response `next`.

settings.title: afbws.account.settings.v2 — DEPRECATED account domain settings (request / response).
settings.description: Deprecated: auto-conversion spread removed; the server does not handle the operation and answers `unsupported_action`. The schema is kept for compatibility. Former behaviour: request `{}` (only `request_id`) reads; `{fx_spread_pct}` writes (staff only, otherwise `forbidden`). Response: `{fx_spread_pct}` — the current spread (percent, decimal string, 0 by default) added to the exchange rate (CETS) on auto-conversion. No server push.

error.title: afbws.account.error.v2 — typed error for a whole request (server -> client).

code.description: The common error codes plus `insufficient_cash` (account.cash withdraw above the balance). `forbidden` and `not_supported` are common codes too.
